inputs.sbc_source: unavailable_not_applicable - full-text search of all FY2018-FY2026 annual and half-year filings confirms Burger Fuel Group has NO share-based payment / equity incentive scheme. SBC is genuinely zero, not undisclosed.

owner_fcf_reconciliation.note_ifrs16_sublease_interest_income: FY2026 P&L shows 'Interest Income - IFRS16 non-occupied leases' of $0.7855m which is EXACTLY offset by an equal 'Interest Expense leases non-occupied' of $0.7855m (sublease pass-through to franchisees). This pair nets to zero real cash effect and is correctly excluded from both the interest-income strip and the FCF adjustment - it is not double counted and not additionally deducted.
owner_fcf_reconciliation.note_ponsonby_gain: The $288K FY2026 one-off gain on the Ponsonby store sale ($140K asset gain + $148K IFRS16 lease-wind-down benefit) is a NON-CASH gain recognized only in the P&L/segment revenue line ('Ponsonby store sale lease adjustment' $147,644). BFG's cash flow statement is prepared under the DIRECT method (Receipts from customers, Payments to suppliers, etc.), not reconciled from Net Profit, so this non-cash gain does not appear in and does not distort reported operating cash flow / FCF at all. The real cash effect (PP&E sale proceeds of $281,708) is already captured correctly in investing activities. No further FCF adjustment for this item was required; it is normalized out of NetIncome/EPS commentary only.
owner_fcf_reconciliation.note_legal_costs: FY2024 (~$205.5K) and FY2025 (~$221.7K) legal costs relating to the contested capital-return scheme of arrangement were real cash SG&A costs already reflected in those years' reported OCF/FCF - explaining why FY2024/FY2025 owner FCF ($1.132m / $0.439m) was depressed relative to FY2026 ($1.915m). FY2026's year-on-year profit jump (+91.8%) is therefore partly just the absence of a one-off drag, not underlying growth, and was NOT extrapolated forward in the base case.
owner_fcf_reconciliation.note_franchisee_lending: BFG makes small recurring net loans to franchisees (FY2024 -$1.8K net, FY2025 -$71.4K net, FY2026 -$289.9K net, all in investing activities) to support network fit-outs. Modelled forward as a small recurring cash drag (~1.0-1.5% of revenue) in the component build since it has been consistently negative and material relative to the small owner-FCF base; this materially closes the gap between an EBITDA-only component build (~9.9% margin) and the FY2026 raw reported-FCF-based owner margin (7.7%).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: SEVERE: Revenue is essentially flat over 8 years (FY2018 $24.774m to FY2026 $24.845m, 0.04% CAGR). EPS and FCF CAGRs shown above (31-46% and 11-30%) are statistical artifacts of a depressed FY2023/24 or FY2024/25 base recovering to a normalized FY2026, combined with the 30% share-count reduction from the June-2024 capital return (50.337m to 35.236m shares) - they are NOT indicative of a growth trajectory and must not be used as the DCF driver. Equity CAGR is similarly distorted by the same capital return (a $4.33m cash outflow that mechanically shrinks book value independent of trading performance). Per management's own FY2027 guidance ('roughly flat' system sales, 'far more challenging operating environment'), the DCF growth driver used is revenue/system-sales trend of approximately 0-2% per year, not any of the CAGRs above.
historical_growth.notes: Total System Sales (the network-wide KPI, not Group revenue) grew 2.93% in FY2026 to $111.4m, roughly consistent with the flat-to-low-single-digit revenue history. FY2024 and FY2025 net income were depressed ~$205.5K and ~$221.7K respectively by non-recurring legal costs from the contested scheme-of-arrangement capital return; FY2026's 91.8% profit growth is a normalization off that depressed base plus a $288K non-cash one-off gain, not organic acceleration.

bull.narrative: New store pipeline (Huapai Sep-2026, Richmond Nelson Nov-2026) executes well; White Label online-ordering platform is commercialised into an incremental higher-margin revenue stream; Shake Out virtual-kitchen expansion continues at +20%/yr pace; no recurrence of governance/legal costs.

bear.narrative: Management's flagged beef/fuel/ingredient cost inflation compresses franchisor and franchisee margins; NZ hospitality discretionary spend softens further; Middle East system sales continue to shrink (-26% in FY2026) toward zero; Winner Winner is wound down; renewed governance/shareholder friction around the ~66% controlling holder resurfaces legal costs.

wacc_rationale.notes: Market cap ~NZ$11.3m is a nano-cap by any definition; Mason Roberts Holdings/Josef Roberts control ~66% of shares, leaving minority holders without effective control and with demonstrated litigation risk (the FY2023-24 scheme-of-arrangement dispute, in which the High Court found 'process failures' even while approving the scheme); the business is a single small domestic market (NZ ~97% of system sales) discretionary-dining franchisor with input-cost and consumer-spending cyclicality. Bull case WACC reduced 1pp (16.0%) to reflect lower perceived execution/governance risk if growth initiatives succeed; bear case WACC raised 1.5pp (18.5%) to reflect elevated risk if margins compress and governance friction resurfaces.

valuation.multiple_expansion_flag: Current EV/OwnerFCF is only ~2.69x (EV $5.14m / owner FCF $1.915m) against a base-case implied exit multiple of 6.80x. The DCF therefore assumes meaningful multiple re-rating from today's distressed/illiquid nano-cap pricing back toward a more normal small-cap franchisor multiple (still well below the ~12-18x more liquid QSR franchisors trade at). This is defensible given the extreme illiquidity discount embedded in the current price, but is a material assumption and is flagged here rather than buried in the model.

base.entry_price_cap_note: WACC (17.0%) exceeds the 15% IRR hurdle rate for this stock, which is unusual (most companies in this repo have WACC below 15%) but appropriate given BFG's nano-cap/illiquidity/concentration risk stack. Discounting the same cash flows at 15% instead of 17% produces a higher PV (uncapped entry price $0.6131) than the intrinsic value itself ($0.5847) - mathematically correct but economically meaningless, since paying full intrinsic value already delivers an expected return equal to WACC (17%), which exceeds the 15% hurdle. Entry price is therefore CAPPED at intrinsic value: an investor should never pay more than fair value chasing a return target below the stock's own required return.

sanity_check.position_description: Current price sits at the extreme BOTTOM of its 10-year trading range (0.57th percentile of the $0.29-$5.567 range), not the upper half.
sanity_check.trip_condition: upside > 100% AND price in upper half of 10yr range
sanity_check.trip_condition_explanation: Base upside (82.7%) is below the 100% threshold, and the price is at the bottom (not upper half) of its range, so the sanity-check trip condition correctly does NOT fire despite the large percentage upside. The large upside reflects a genuinely depressed nano-cap price (P/E 5.4x, P/S 0.43x, P/B 0.89x, EV/OwnerFCF 2.7x, market cap NZ$11.3m against $11.8m of equity and $6.1m of cash with zero debt) rather than an unreasonable model assumption.

historical_multiples_reconciliation.methodology_note: Share counts changed materially over the history due to the June-2024 capital return (30% of shares cancelled, 50.337m to 35.236m). Historical P/E, P/S, P/B below use the SHARE COUNT CONTEMPORANEOUS WITH EACH PERIOD's price (50.337m for FY2018/FY2020-FY2024, 53.670m for FY2019, 35.236m for FY2025-FY2026) so market cap in each year is correctly computed, avoiding the trap of mixing a pre-cancellation share count with a post-cancellation price. The CSV's raw EPS column is in CENTS per NZX convention and was NOT used directly; EPS below is derived as NetIncome / contemporaneous SharesOutstanding.
historical_multiples_reconciliation.caution: The FY2024-to-FY2025 price drop ($0.450 to $0.340, -24.4%) partly reflects the 30% capital return / share cancellation implemented in June 2024 (NZ$0.27/share paid for cancelled shares), which is a return OF capital, not a value decline - the per-share metrics above already correctly use the post-cancellation share count from FY2025 onward, so P/E, P/S and P/B are NOT distorted by mixing mismatched share counts, but the raw price series alone should not be read as a pure valuation derating without this context.
historical_multiples_reconciliation.conclusion: P/E has compressed from 50-110x (FY2019-2023, when profits were tiny and volatile) to 5.4-11.7x (FY2025-2026, on materially higher and more normalized profit). P/B has fallen from 5-7x to under 1x (now trading BELOW book value at 0.89-0.95x). P/S has fallen from 3-6x to 0.43-0.50x. All three multiples corroborate that BFG is priced at a substantial discount to any historical valuation norm and below liquidation/book value, consistent with (a) extreme nano-cap illiquidity, (b) the concentrated/litigious register, and (c) two years of depressed reported earnings only now normalizing - not with a fundamentally impaired business (revenue flat but resilient, zero debt, net cash position, best-ever NPAT in FY2026).

valuation_philosophy.summary: BurgerFuel Group is a tiny, ex-growth, single-market (NZ ~97% of system sales) royalty/franchise business trading at a deep discount to both book value and any historical multiple, reflecting extreme nano-cap illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$11.3m) and a concentrated, litigious ownership register (Mason Roberts Holdings/Josef Roberts ~66%) rather than fundamental business impairment. The DCF is built bottom-up from FY2026 (the cleanest recent year - net of both the FY2024/25 legal-cost drag and any assumption that the $288K Ponsonby one-off gain repeats) using a component EBITDA-to-owner-FCF build, NOT a flat FCF-margin carry-forward and NOT the 91.8% FY2026 profit growth rate, which management itself does not expect to repeat (FY2027 system sales guided 'roughly flat' amid 'a far more challenging operating environment').
key_judgment_calls: SBC is confirmed genuinely zero (no share-based payment scheme exists) - the owner-FCF adjustment is therefore driven entirely by stripping bank interest income (net cash > 1x FCF base) and deducting the real IFRS-16 lease principal cash outflow BFG's operating cash flow statement excludes.

The offsetting IFRS-16 sublease interest income/expense pair ($0.7855m each side) nets to zero and was correctly excluded from any adjustment - treating it as strippable income would have overstated the interest-income deduction by roughly 5x.

The Ponsonby $288K gain required NO FCF adjustment because BFG's cash flow statement uses the direct method and was never inflated by this non-cash P&L item in the first place - only NetIncome/EPS commentary needed normalizing.

Revenue/system-sales growth (not equity, EPS or FCF CAGR, all of which are distorted by the FY2024 capital return and/or the legal-cost swing) is the DCF growth driver, at a conservative 0-2%/yr matching management's own flat guidance and the 8-year 0.04% revenue CAGR.

WACC (17% base) is built as an explicit 4-layer stack (NZ small-cap base + nano-cap illiquidity + register-concentration + single-market cyclicality) per the mandated methodology, landing in the 'high teens' as directed.
Entry price is capped at intrinsic value because WACC (17%) exceeds the 15% IRR hurdle here - an unusual but correct edge case for this risk profile.

The valuation implies material multiple expansion (2.7x to 6.8x EV/OwnerFCF) from today's distressed pricing; this is flagged explicitly rather than assumed silently, and even so the resulting fair value (~$0.58) remains at only ~7x FY2026 owner FCF and below FY2025/2026 book value multiples seen historically.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Base case intrinsic value NZ$0.58 (+82.7%), bull NZ$0.74 (+132.6%), bear NZ$0.41 (+27.8%), probability-weighted NZ$0.58 (+81.5%) against a current price of NZ$0.32. Even the bear case, which assumes margin compression from input-cost inflation and a shrinking Middle East book, sits comfortably above the current price - because the current price embeds an illiquidity/governance discount so severe the stock trades below net cash plus a single year's EBITDA. This is a classic net-cash, sub-book-value NZX micro-cap where the thesis is 'the business isn't dying, the float is just tiny and nobody's covering it' rather than a high-growth compounder story.
